content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use feel and have with a few common symptoms. Model: “I feel tired, and I have a mild headache today.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use how do you feel? clearly and politely. One useful response is: “I feel tired, and I have a mild headache today.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where how do you feel? is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Complete the natural sentence about how do you feel?: I feel tired, and I have _____ today.
Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about how do you feel?.
Make a short, personal response about how do you feel?. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about how do you feel?.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Use feel and have with a few common symptoms.
objectives: Use feel and have with a few common symptoms.
Use basic health words in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about how do you feel?.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about how do you feel?. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: How does the speaker feel?
listening.transcript: I have a headache, so I feel tired today.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Stress HEAD-ache and TIRED; keep have a linked. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Stress HEAD-ache and TIRED; keep have a linked.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about how do you feel?.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using how do you feel?; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise how do you feel??” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: I feel tired, and I have a mild headache today.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about how do you feel? with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about how do you feel?. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: I feel tired, and I have a mild headache today. Submit your draft first.

title: How do you feel?
